summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of chronic obstructive lung disease, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted after being found unconscious with severe hypoxia. He was treated for an acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, likely due to pneumonia, and received oxygen therapy and antibiotics. Given his history of delirium tremens and high benzodiazepine requirements, he was managed for alcohol withdrawal with Valium. He reported hematemesis, raising concern for gastrointestinal complications of chronic alcohol use. Despite clinical improvement, he elected to leave against medical advice after a brief hospitalization. At discharge, he was stable on oxygen, with controlled withdrawal symptoms, and was provided prescriptions and follow-up instructions.
problems: Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, unspecified
